meta.ogDescription: Wikiquote sources it to a 1997 Martyn Lewis interview book. The book is real; its text was not reachable to check.

answer.label: Attributed to
answer.authorDates: b. 1950 · English entrepreneur, founder of the Virgin Group
answer.sourceLine: Credibly Branson’s, with a named source we could not open. Wikiquote attributes it to an interview he gave Martyn Lewis ↗ for the book Reflections on Success (1997) — a real, catalogued book, but one whose scanned copy is lending-restricted, so we could not read the page. Note too that the quotation usually stops a clause early: it carries on, “And, quite often, just out of personal frustration about the way it’s been done by other people.”

source.heading: The source

docMeta.dd: Lennard, 1997 · the Internet Archive holds a 1998 printing
Attributed — source named, but not opened

source.excerpt: “I became an entrepreneur by mistake. Ever since then I’ve gone into business, not to make money, but because I think I can do it better than it’s been done elsewhere. And, quite often, just out of personal frustration about the way it’s been done by other people.”
trail: Wikiquote gives both the fullest text and the only specific source anyone offers for it: an interview with Martyn Lewis in his book Reflections on Success (1997) ↗.

The book is real. The Internet Archive catalogues Martyn Lewis, Reflections on Success: famous achievers talk frankly to Martyn Lewis about their route to the top ↗ (Harpenden: Lennard), 960 pages, ISBN 1852911395 — and its record notes “Previous edition: 1997,” which matches the date Wikiquote gives.

And confirmed from a second direction. Wikipedia’s article on Martyn Lewis ↗ independently lists Reflections on Success (1997) among his books, describing it as “interviews with more than 60 notable individuals across a wide range of professions analysing their success” — which matches both the date and the kind of book Wikiquote cites.

What we could not do. That scanned copy is lending-restricted, so its text cannot be searched, and no other full text of the book was reachable. The quotation is credibly sourced but not confirmed word for word against the page.
source.excerptNote: This is the wording Wikiquote prints, including the third sentence the popular version drops. We have not seen the printed page, so treat the sentence boundaries as Wikiquote’s rather than as confirmed from the book.
source.rightsNote: A 1997 interview with a living author, published in a book still in copyright. Nothing here is public domain. Because we have not opened the source, we name Branson as the speaker rather than asserting which publisher holds the printed text.

author.name: Richard Branson
author.heading: Who said it
author.metaLine: born 1950 · English entrepreneur · founder of the Virgin Group
author.bio: Sir Richard Charles Nicholas Branson was born in Blackheath, London, in 1950, is dyslexic, and left Stowe School at sixteen to start a magazine called Student. A mail-order record business followed in 1970 and the first Virgin Records shop in 1972; the brand later carried an airline, a rail franchise and a spaceflight company. He was knighted in 2000 for services to entrepreneurship.

misattribution.heading: What gets lost in the quoting
misattribution.intro: Nobody else is claiming these words. What goes missing is the end of them — and, in most reprints, any source at all.

items.who: the version that stops at “done elsewhere”
items.why: Wikiquote ↗ continues: “And, quite often, just out of personal frustration about the way it’s been done by other people.” The dropped clause is the one that names what actually sets him off.

items.who: the reprints that give no source at all
items.why: Most sites carry the line bare. The one specific citation on offer is Wikiquote’s — an interview with Martyn Lewis ↗ for Reflections on Success ↗ — and we could not open the book to check it.

misattribution.truthLine: Wikiquote’s full text: “I became an entrepreneur by mistake. Ever since then I’ve gone into business, not to make money, but because I think I can do it better than it’s been done elsewhere. And, quite often, just out of personal frustration about the way it’s been done by other people.” — Richard Branson on Wikiquote ↗

context.heading: Why it mattered
lead: “By mistake” is doing some work here. Wikipedia’s account ↗ is that Branson “expressed his desire to become an entrepreneur at a young age” and started his first business, the magazine Student, at sixteen — then a mail-order record business in 1970 and the first Virgin Records shop in 1972. Whether any of that counts as an accident depends on how generously you read the word.

The rest of the sentence is the part worth keeping: not for the money, but because he thought he could do the thing better than the people already doing it. That is the claim the Virgin name has been testing ever since, across records, an airline, a rail franchise and a spaceflight company.
detailsBody: Martyn Lewis (born 1945) is a broadcast journalist who read the news for ITN from 1970 and then for the BBC from 1986 to 1999. Wikipedia’s account of his books ↗ describes Reflections on Success (1997) as “interviews with more than 60 notable individuals across a wide range of professions analysing their success.” The Internet Archive’s copy runs to 960 pages.

sourcesVerified.claim: Wikiquote's Richard Branson page carries the three-sentence form of this quotation and sources it: “As stated in an interview with Martyn Lewis in his book, Reflections on Success (1997)”.

The Internet Archive catalogue record for Reflections on Success gives creator “Lewis, Martyn, 1945-”, publisher “Harpenden : Lennard”, date 1998, 960 pages, ISBN 1852911395, and the note “Previous edition: 1997”. The item is access-restricted, so its text could not be searched.

Wikipedia states Branson “expressed his desire to become an entrepreneur at a young age” and that his first business venture, at sixteen, was a magazine called Student, followed by a mail-order record business in 1970 and Virgin Records stores in 1972.

Wikipedia's Martyn Lewis article gives his birth year as 1945, his career as ITN (1970-1986) then BBC (1986-1999) news presenting, and lists among his books “Reflections on Success (1997) – interviews with more than 60 notable individuals across a wide range of professions analysing their success.”
